description: Portable SDK build requirements and host-specific reference configurations. This is not standard machine cloud-init user data.
composition: Both common and a selected host_environments entry are required. Also read its uses_host_environment entry, if present, and add the chosen profile requirements. Profiles provide concrete examples; they do not weaken common requirements or qualify untested hosts. No automatic merge, installation or profile selection is implemented.

common.host_and_target: Select host OS and CPU independently from the target architecture and triplet. Native compilers and generators must execute on the selected host; target libraries remain in the sysroot.

path_roles.sources: Clean, fully materialized OS, Ports and SDK source checkouts.
path_roles.workspace: Target-specific Prebuild SDK, prepared pkgsrc export, verified libedit source, objects, stages and receipts.
path_roles.cache: Verified source archives and downloaded native packages.
path_roles.temporary: Temporary files and native configuration probes.
path_roles.host_tools: Selected SDK native tool and interpreter prefix with recorded producer provenance; a path or symlink alone does not establish membership.

sdk_control.python: CPython 3.15 with its standard library, including ctypes and POSIX process modules

native_and_ports_build.base_compilers: Use SDK native GCC16 for host programs and SDK cross GCC16 for target code. Select all build tools through the SDK policy in docs/tool-selection.md. Host ABI headers and libraries must be explicit recorded inputs; system compiler fallback is forbidden.

ports_host_compilers.requirement: The current GCC16 cross recipe requires host-executable GCC and G++ major version 16; Clang is not a substitute for this recipe.
ports_host_compilers.provider: Use the qualified SDK native GCC16 provider and record absolute paths and provenance. Ambient PATH defaults and system package installation are not approved substitutes.

native_and_ports_build.sdk_final_host_compilers: Require explicit SDK native GCC16 selection. The current sysroot and release builders search PATH for cc and c++; this is an enforcement gap. Repair the common selector and refusal checks before accepting builds that depend on it.

header_rpc_preprocessor.when: Install OS headers before the target compiler is available.
header_rpc_preprocessor.command: The selected SDK native GCC16 preprocessor as one absolute executable path
header_rpc_preprocessor.selection: Set TOOL_RPCGEN for the includes invocation to RPCGEN_CPP=<native-cpp> <native-nbrpcgen>. Preserve the target CPP setting for later library builds.
header_rpc_preprocessor.evidence: Record the native preprocessor and its executed components. Check the generated rpcb_prot.h declarations required by libc.

native_and_ports_build.generated_make: OS native tools provide nbmake and a host GNU make. Use the GNU make provider and selector accepted by the selected Ports entry point.
native_and_ports_build.host_math: Ports builds GMP 6.3.0, MPFR 4.2.2 and MPC 1.4.1 from its pinned sources.
native_and_ports_build.optional_ports_profiles: Additional profiles retain their upstream tools, such as CMake or LLVM build dependencies. They are not SDK Python imports.

python_source_bootstrap.when: CPython 3.15 is not already available for the selected host
python_source_bootstrap.source: Official CPython source; verify the selected release and commit.

required_module_support.ctypes: The native foreign-function library and development files needed by the selected CPython build, normally libffi.
required_module_support.ssl: Compatible OpenSSL development files and certificate trust for the Ports HTTPS download path.
required_module_support.posix: The selected host's native development tools and POSIX process interfaces.

producer_specific_module_support.zlib: Required for libedit source preparation and when Ports runtime relink recovery reads its gzip-compressed backup through Python tarfile.

python_source_bootstrap.platform_module_providers: Optional uuid and database modules use the providers available on the selected host; a separate package is not required when the system supplies them.
python_source_bootstrap.scope: SDK control requires its imported standard-library modules, including ctypes and POSIX process support. Ports HTTPS downloads also need ssl. Optional module coverage does not establish or limit unrelated SDK build capabilities.

tools: Ruby with JSON, YAML and Minitest
optional_repository_validation.scope: OS and Ports repository validators; not SDK Python imports.

optional_source_analysis.scope: Development checks for compatible native C programs. These tools do not establish target execution acceptance.

read_system: Native executables, development headers and libraries
HTTPS certificates and selected source/package trust metadata
capabilities: Relative symbolic links; builds must work on case-insensitive paths
Executable file modes and native execution from build paths
Exclusive creation, atomic rename, fsync and POSIX flock
filesystem.path_constraints: Use real absolute paths without whitespace. Keep source inputs separate from writable build outputs.

operations: Spawn native subprocesses and create POSIX sessions
Inspect process identities and signal owned same-UID session members
Wait for and reap owned child processes
process.scope: Producers retain their effective UID and session. The selected native backend must prove that owned writers have stopped before releasing build locks.
process.restriction_policy: The selected host backend adds its native visibility and API requirements. Missing capabilities fail preflight or ownership verification.

network.purpose: Acquire public source checkouts, pinned archives and signed native packages.
network.host_provider_policy: Add the selected native tool or package provider's endpoints in the concrete host profile. This description does not install a network allowlist.
network.integrity: Verify source commits and Ports archive hashes. Verify native packages with the selected provider's signed metadata and checksums.
network.offline: Existing verified inputs can be reused without downloading them.

privilege.conditions: Native tools and source inputs are already accessible; outputs use caller-owned paths and unprivileged OS staging.
privilege.host_provisioning: Installing a host OS, WSL2, development tools or system packages can require separate administrator permissions. They are not producer permissions.

resources.minimums: Not established. Size disk space for source archives, independent build trees, installed stages and receipts.
resources.selection: Choose jobs and disk capacity for the actual host. Reference allocations do not establish portable minimums.

common.acceptance: Keep filesystem/process contracts, actual compiler and sysroot builds, cross-link checks and EmberBSD target execution as separate evidence. A listed architecture or passing preflight is not complete build qualification.

requirements.filesystem: Readable /proc enumeration and PID stat/status records for the current PID namespace, including identities needed to account for owned descendants.
process: PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER in each private Python supervisor
Reap producer descendants in their private supervisor without changing the controller subreaper setting
requirements.native_tools: Provide Linux executables and development libraries for the host CPU and libc. Select a distribution package provider or a verified native source build.

qualification.x86_64: Filesystem, process and fixture-producer contracts were checked on Linux 6.18 with CPython 3.15. Ports also documents Debian x86_64 kernel cross-compiler checks.
qualification.aarch64: The Linux backend has no CPU selector. Native ARM64 tool availability and actual filesystem, process and complete build checks are still required on that host.
qualification.complete_build: Require receipts for the selected distribution, host CPU, tool versions, target and source revisions.

process: Base-system ps with pid, ppid, uid and stat fields
Public proc_pid_rusage RUSAGE_INFO_V0 and mach_absolute_time through standard-library ctypes and /usr/lib/libproc.dylib
requirements.native_tools: Provide native development tools, a compatible macOS SDK and host-executable GCC/G++16 for the Ports GCC16 recipe.
requirements.sdk_selection: The documented Ports workflow uses SDKROOT when host GCC cannot locate system libraries. xcrun --show-sdk-path selects the installed macOS SDK.
requirements.filesystem: Use a build filesystem with the common link and executable-mode capabilities. Builds must work on case-insensitive filesystems, such as the default APFS volume.

qualification.arm64: The SDK documents initial workspace contracts on macOS arm64. Ports documents AArch64 application cross-compiler checks on Apple Silicon macOS.
qualification.x86_64: The Darwin backend has no CPU selector. The selected native tools and actual contracts still need host-specific checks.
qualification.complete_build: These scoped results do not establish a fresh complete SDK build for arbitrary macOS versions or host CPUs.

requirements.execution: Run Python, Git, SDK/Ports controllers and every native build tool inside the selected WSL2 Linux distribution. Select executables for the Linux guest architecture, not Windows .exe files.
requirements.filesystem: Require symbolic links, executable modes and locks for sources and build outputs. Builds must work on case-insensitive paths. The Linux guest filesystem is recommended. Windows-mounted paths such as /mnt/c require validation of the same properties; their location alone establishes neither compatibility nor incompatibility.
requirements.process: The actual WSL2 kernel and security settings must satisfy all Linux process backend requirements.

wsl2.qualification: The Linux backend is available to the guest. ARM64 and x86_64 WSL2 distributions still require their own actual contracts and full SDK build checks; bare Linux results do not qualify WSL2.

native-windows.qualification: No native Windows producer backend or binary SDK is qualified. Current OS/Ports producers require POSIX tools. Windows Python workspace inspection alone does not qualify a build.
native-windows.current_route: Use the WSL2 Linux guest requirements, subject to their pending qualification.

qualification.process_backend: Native Linux filesystem and process contracts passed with CPython 3.15.
qualification.complete_build: Requires successful compiler, runtime, sysroot and cross-link receipts for the selected inputs.

dependencies.base_compilers: Historical observation only: Debian 13 GCC14 produced native bootstrap and CPython builds. This does not authorize new builds; the current policy requires the qualified SDK native GCC16 provider.
dependencies.header_rpc_preprocessor: The reference selects native cpp-16 during the includes step and records its wrapper, driver and cc1 hashes.
dependencies.sdk_final_host_compilers: Historical observation only: this reference used PATH cc and c++ from GCC14. It does not satisfy the current SDK tool policy. Replace this provider through the common SDK selector and verify native GCC16 before a new build.
dependencies.generated_make: OS native tools provide nbmake and nbgmake. The reference nbgmake is GNU Make 3.81.

private_debian_package_extraction.policy: Use packages compatible with the base host. Extract into host_tools; retain the system loader and libc.

python_source_bootstrap.source: Official CPython v3.15.0; record its verified source commit and executable hash.
python_source_bootstrap.scope: Observed module checks for this reference interpreter, not a complete optional-module build.

network.integrity: Verify signed Debian repository metadata and downloaded package hashes.

privilege.conditions: Native packages are extracted into a caller-owned prefix; OS installation uses unprivileged staging.

reference.scope: Observed host allocation, not a completed SDK build qualification.

resources.minimums: Not established. Size disk space for source archives, independent build trees, installed stages and receipts.
